results.title: The use of a deep learning technique called Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) to predict a sequence \(H\) (\(H = 6\)) of numerical values of the time difference UTC-UTC(\(k\)) for different UTC(\(k\)) timescales. It is found that, in general, the predicted values “follow” true UTC(\(k\)) values published on the z Circular T document. Results obtained with the GRU technique are encouraging when they are compared with other standard deep learning algorithms such as LSTM, 1D CNN, and MLP. GRU predictions are better for some timescales than others. We consider that, among other factors, human interventions on the UTC(\(k\)) operation increase the difficulty of the GRU to predict true values. In that sense, human interventions act as an unpredictable factor. Furthermore, we discussed the possibility of using GRU predicted results to correct in advance “future” deviations of the timescales with respect to the UTC. In any case, GRU results are encouraging and confirm the possibility of using the predictions to improve the UTC(\(k\)) timescale performance.
